## AI as a Mathematical Collaborator {.opening-slide}

::: {.eyebrow}
MATH4SDG · UDSM · SATURDAY 21 NOVEMBER 2026
:::

::: {.lead-subtitle}
Build two models. Question the AI. Test the evidence.
:::

::: {.big-question}
**Can we reconstruct missing weather measurements without looking into the future?**
:::

::: {.time-cue}
60-minute student workshop · work alone or in pairs
:::



## Two stations, incomplete observations

::: {.eyebrow}
THE MATHEMATICAL PROBLEM · 2–6 MIN
:::

::: {.slide-subtitle}
Estimate missing temperatures at A or B using available information.
:::

::: {.small-results}
| Day | A (°C) | B (°C) | Humidity | Wind |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|:--|
| 1 | 28.5 | 28.1 | available | available |
| 2 | **missing** | 29.0 | available | available |
| 3 | **missing** | **missing** | available | available |
| 4 | 30.1 | **missing** | available | available |
:::

::: {.takeaway}
**Allowed:** measurements from today and earlier days. **Not allowed:** later measurements or concealed answers.
:::



## Open the activity in JupyterLab

::: {.eyebrow}
STUDENT ACTION · 6–12 MIN
:::

::: {.activity-steps}
1. Extract the **Saturday student update ZIP** shared by the facilitator.
2. Copy its notebook into the existing **notebooks/** folder and its three CSVs into **data/exercises/**. **Do not replace the folders.**
3. In the **left JupyterLab file browser**, double-click **notebooks**, then double-click **ai_assisted_weather_modelling.ipynb**.
4. Run code cells with **Shift + Enter**. Explore the data, completion rule and baseline.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Keep JupyterLab and your AI assistant open side by side. **No new installation.**
:::



## Ask AI for two different models

::: {.eyebrow}
INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION · 12–32 MIN
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
::: {.model-card}
**First model · 10 min**

Ask AI for a simple predictor.

**first_predict_temperature**

Run it. Record the validation MAE.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="49%"}
::: {.model-card}
**Second model · 10 min**

Ask AI for a different mathematical approach.

**second_predict_temperature**

Run it on the **same validation cases**.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Only **earlier training rows** and **one prediction case** may be used. No global data, hidden answers or future observations.
:::



## Now challenge your AI assistant

::: {.eyebrow}
CRITICISM AND COMPARISON · 32–43 MIN
:::

::: {.activity-steps}
1. **Compare:** Which mathematical assumptions differ between the models?
2. **Criticize:** How could either fail during missing observations or on new days?
3. **Verify:** Independently check **one AI-generated claim**.
4. **Optional:** Make one change, then measure validation MAE again.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
More complicated—or more convincing-sounding—does not necessarily mean more accurate.
:::



## Choose first. Reveal second.

::: {.eyebrow}
FINAL TEST · 43–48 MIN
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
::: {.model-card}
**1. Lock your choice**

Compare the baseline and both AI models.

Assign **chosen_predict_temperature** to the chosen function.

*Record why you chose it.*
:::
:::

::: {.column width="49%"}
::: {.model-card}
**2. Test once**

The facilitator reveals the **deobfuscation function**.

Complete **deobfuscation(x)** in JupyterLab.

Compare the final-test MAE with the baseline.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Do not change the selected model after seeing the final-test result.
:::
